study_identification.title: Lifespan Normative Models of White Matter Fractional Anisotropy: Applications to Early Psychosis

study_characteristics.study_objective: The study aims to: (i) develop large-scale normative models of Fractional Anisotropy (FA) across the lifespan using data from over 25,000 healthy individuals; (ii) apply these models to an early psychosis cohort to investigate white matter heterogeneity and individual deviations; (iii) demonstrate multi-modal data fusion by combining FA deviations with structural brain measures to identify biological signatures of psychosis symptoms; and (iv) release the models publicly.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: A multi-view sparse canonical correlation analysis (msCCA) was used to identify multivariate associations between three 'views': (1) symptom domains (PANSS scores), (2) FA deviations, and (3) structural deviations (cortical thickness and subcortical volume). The analysis aimed to maximize the correlation between symptoms and the neuroimaging modalities.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study developed large-scale normative models of FA, revealing significant, individualized white matter heterogeneity in early psychosis not visible in group-level analyses, and demonstrated that multimodal deviations predict symptom severity.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: While no significant case-control differences in mean FA deviations survived FDR correction, individuals with psychosis showed a significantly greater proportion of extreme positive and negative Z-scores, indicating high inter-individual heterogeneity. A multi-view sparse canonical correlation analysis (msCCA) linking symptom scores with brain deviations yielded a significant canonical correlation (r=0.25). The association was driven by cognitive and total PANSS scores, and the most predictive features were FA in the right uncinate fasciculus and bilateral thalamus volume.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study's limitations include a skewed age distribution in the reference cohort with gaps in early childhood and old age; unexplored variability from demographic factors like socioeconomic status; and a training dataset biased towards 'WEIRD' populations, for which self-reported race is an imperfect proxy for ethnicity.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: A key innovation is the use of multi-view sparse canonical correlation analysis (msCCA) to fuse deviation data from multiple imaging modalities (dMRI, sMRI) and link them to clinical symptom dimensions. The study also emphasizes open science by making all developed normative models publicly available through the PCNtoolkit and a dedicated GitHub repository.

general_notes.general_notes: There is a discrepancy in the number of control participants in the clinical application section. The text mentions n=55 controls from the HCP-EP dataset, but Supplementary Table S2 reports N=28. The reference cohort was constructed from the following datasets: Human Connectome Project (HCP) Baby, HCP Development, HCP Young Adult, HCP Aging, and UK Biobank.
